summary: Configured inventory-worker as an enabled, long-running systemd service on node1. It runs under a dedicated unprivileged account, can write only within /var/lib/inventory, and has NoNewPrivileges enabled. The service and its confinement recovered successfully after a verified node reboot.
actions_performed: Created the inventory-worker system account and protected data directory.
Installed and enabled inventory-worker.service with a read-only filesystem except /var/lib/inventory, an empty capability set, and NoNewPrivileges=yes.
Tested that writes succeed inside /var/lib/inventory and fail under /var/lib, /etc, and /tmp.
Safely rebooted node1 and verified its boot identity changed.
Confirmed the service, heartbeat data, privilege restriction, and filesystem confinement recovered after reboot.

evidence.requirement: inventory-worker is a managed, enabled, long-running service
evidence.summary: Systemd reports the unit enabled and active; its heartbeat demonstrates ongoing work.
Tests within the service mount namespace allowed writes in /var/lib/inventory while denying writes to /var/lib, /etc, and /tmp, both before and after reboot.
Systemd reports NoNewPrivileges=yes, the live process reports NoNewPrivs: 1, and the capability bounding set is empty.

Captured healthy baseline boot ID 4b43f122-6c8b-4c87-b01a-12705c4a9f4f, acknowledged the native reboot, then observed changed boot ID 1a102212-3901-4d89-ad6b-174de6966e6e with the system running and the enabled worker, changing heartbeat, NoNewPrivileges, and confinement fully recovered.
